text.p: Dominik Hasek made 31 saves for his second straight shutout and Derek Plante scored twice as the Buffalo Sabres blanked the Ottawa Senators, 3-0 on Friday.
"It's a great feeling (getting the shutout), but our defence played well," Hasek said. (Ottawa) came hard. They had a couple of good chances to score.
"We are a tired hockey club," said Sabres coach Ted Nolan. "We wanted to come out strong and have a good first period and let character take over and get the win, and that is exactly what we did."

In Anaheim, Guy Hebert recorded his second shutout in seven days and Paul Kariya had a goal and an assist as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim blanked the slumping Chicago Blackhawks, 2-0 for their third win in four games.
Hebert made 27 saves for his 11th career shutout. Kariya, who has three goals and four assists in his last five games, scored the only goal Hebert needed at 15:03 of the first period.
In Boston, Jozef Stumpel and Steve Heinze each had two goals and an assist to lead the Boston Bruins to a 7-3 rout of the Vancouver Canucks.

Stumpel scored twice in a four-goal first period that was capped by Heinze's first goal of the game with 49 seconds left. Heinze added a power-play goal with 1:23 left in the second period to make it 6-2 as the Bruins completed a two-game season sweep of Vancouver.
"Everyone played well. We played well away from the puck," Stumpel said. "We have to play good defence to win and we knew how fast and talented the Canucks are.
At Florida, Keith Primeau scored on a breakaway 9:57 into the third period to lift the Hartford Whalers into a 1-1 tie with the Florida Panthers.
"I saw it go in, I went to flick it over his glove and I missed it, but he didn't get back in time," Primeau said. "This was a very gritty effort. ... That's been lacking in the last few games."
Sean Burke made 29 saves for the Whalers.
In San Jose, Ryan Smyth scored the go-ahead goal with 59 seconds left in the first period and the Edmonton Oilers held on for their third straight road win, 4-2 over the San Jose Sharks.
Edmonton has outscored opponents, 18-3, in its recent road success.

With the score tied, 2-2, Smyth took a pass low in the right faceoff circle from Mariusz Czerkawski. Smyth skated around the back of the net and waited for goaltender Kelly Hrudey to go down before lifting a shot just under the crossbar for his 12th goal of the season.
Ulf Dahlen and Greg Hawgood scored power-play goals for the Sharks.

At Tampa Bay, Arturs Irbe stopped 29 shots for his first win in six weeks and Jamie Langenbrunner and Sergei Zubov scored first-period goals to give the Dallas Stars a 2-1 victory over the floundering Tampa Bay Lightning.

"We realised they were very desperate coming into tonight, not only by their record, but because they were playing at home," said Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock. "We really wanted to come out strong tonight."
Langenbrunner put Dallas ahead to stay with a power-play goal at 9:48 of the first period.
In Washington, Tommy Salo recorded his first career shutout and red-hot Zigmund Palffy scored both goals as the New York Islanders blanked the Washington Capitals, 2-0.
Salo made 23 saves, including 12 in the third period, for the Islanders' first road shutout since Ron Hextall whitewashed Tampa Bay on April 13th, 1994.
"Yes, I am going to keep that puck and will remember it when I am retired one day," Salo said.
